title: Drosophila Embryo Collection Protocol
author: Katy M Monteith
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.k9dcz26

steps.title: Prepare apple‑agar plate
steps.instruction: Place an apple‑agar plate in the embryo collection cage, smear a peanut‑butter‑consistency yeast paste (dry yeast mixed with water) onto the centre, and add water‑soaked absorbent cotton wool for moisture.

steps.title: Add flies and incubate
steps.instruction: Introduce the fly population into the cage and incubate at 25 ± 1 °C under a 12 h light : 12 h dark cycle for 24 h.

steps.title: Check egg laying
steps.instruction: Inspect the apple‑agar surface for eggs; if too few, replace with a fresh apple‑agar plate, re‑soak the cotton wool, and continue incubation for an additional 24 h.

steps.title: Collect and clean plate
steps.instruction: Remove the egg‑laden plate, discard remaining yeast paste and any dead flies from the agar surface.

steps.title: Dislodge eggs into PBS
steps.instruction: Submerge the plate in 1x PBS, gently brush eggs off the agar (most are on the outer edge) with a fine paintbrush, transfer the suspension to a Falcon tube, and let stand for 5 min so eggs sink.

steps.title: Transfer egg suspension (p1000)
steps.instruction: Cut 4 mm off the tip of a filtered P1000 pipette, snap‑release the plunger to draw 1 mL of the settled egg suspension from the bottom of the Falcon tube, dispense into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube, and allow to settle.

steps.title: Aliquot desired egg number
steps.instruction: Cut 4 mm off a filtered P20 tip, set the pipette to the desired volume, snap‑release to draw from the bottom of the microcentrifuge tube; 5 μL yields approximately 102 ± 4 eggs.

steps.title: Dispense onto food
steps.instruction: Place the collected eggs onto the appropriate food source and allow development until needed for experiments.
